hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: At 0.50 mg/ml, full-length apoE4 had a larger large-species fraction than apoE3, 26% versus 21%, despite identical weight-average sedimentation coefficients of 6.5 S.
rows.Finding quote: Furthermore, at higher protein concentration, large species ( s > 10) were more significantly increased for the apoE4 protein (by 15%), compared to apoE3 protein (6%). These observations support the greater aggregation of apoE4 protein.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (higher fraction of large apoE species at 0.50 mg/ml)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human full-length apoE3 and apoE4 with C-terminal His tags; PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C and 40,000 rpm. Table 2 specifies that its higher-concentration full-length samples were 0.50 mg/ml.
rows.Data location: Fig 4A–B; Table 2, higher-concentration full-length rows and footnote; Table 1

rows.Finding description: Increasing full-length protein concentration from 0.15 to 0.50 mg/ml increased the large-species fraction by 15 percentage points for apoE4 and 6 percentage points for apoE3.
rows.Finding quote: Furthermore, at higher protein concentration, large species ( s > 10) were more significantly increased for the apoE4 protein (by 15%), compared to apoE3 protein (6%).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater concentration-dependent increase in large apoE species)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human full-length apoE3 and apoE4; PBS, pH 7.3; 0.15 and 0.50 mg/ml; sedimentation velocity at 20°C and 40,000 rpm.
rows.Data location: Fig 4A–B; Table 2; Results, Size distribution of full-length apoE3 and apoE4 proteins

rows.Finding description: At 1.00 mg/ml, apoE4 72–299 had more large species than apoE3 72–299, 21% versus 12%, and a more heterogeneous distribution; the apoE3 major region contained 77% at 5.9 S.
rows.Finding quote: Similar to the full-length proteins, at higher protein concentrations, apoE4 72-299 had more abundant larger species ( s > 10, 21%), compared with those of apoE3 72-299 (12%). ApoE4 72-299 therefore shows a greater tendency to aggregate.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 72–299 -> apoE4 72–299) -> (higher large-species fraction and greater heterogeneity)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 72–299; 1.00 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C and 40,000 rpm; continuous c(s) analysis.
rows.Data location: Fig 4E–F; Table 2, 1.00 mg/ml rows

rows.Finding description: Increasing concentration from 0.15 to 1.00 mg/ml increased the apoE4 72–299 large-species fraction from 7% to 21%, while the apoE3 fraction changed from 13% to 12%.
rows.Finding quote: This feature showed that aggregation of apoE4 72-299 protein was more sensitive to concentration.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 72–299 -> apoE4 72–299) -> (greater concentration-dependent aggregation)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 72–299; 0.15 and 1.00 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C.
rows.Data location: Fig 4E–F; Table 2

rows.Finding description: At 0.15 mg/ml, apoE4 1–271 contained more large species than apoE3 1–271, 21% versus 13%, with overlapping oligomer distributions spanning approximately 50–400 kDa.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE4 1-271 was made up of more and larger species ( s > 10; 21%), compared to apoE3 1-271 (13%).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 1–271 -> apoE4 1–271) -> (higher fraction of large apoE oligomers)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 1–271; 0.15 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C; continuous sedimentation and molar-mass distributions.
rows.Data location: Fig 5A–D, dotted curves; Results, Size distribution of C-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins

rows.Finding description: At 1.0 mg/ml, full-length apoE4 had a larger 5.0–15.0 nm particle fraction than apoE3, 46% versus 35%, while both also had a 3.9 nm particle group.
rows.Finding quote: Both apoE3 and E4 proteins showed a distribution with two major particle groups, one with a size of 3.9 nm and another in the range of 5.0–15.0 nm. However, apoE3 had less 5.0–15.0 nm group particles (35%), compared with those of apoE4 (46%).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (higher fraction of larger apoE particles)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human full-length apoE3 and apoE4; 1.0 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; DynaPro-MS/X dynamic light scattering at 20°C, total detection 30–40 minutes per sample.
rows.Data location: Results, Dynamic light scattering of apoE proteins, full-length comparison

rows.Finding description: ApoE4 72–299 showed a 10.0–25.0 nm large-particle group comprising 36% and a 5.1 nm group comprising 62%, whereas apoE3 72–299 had one major 4–10 nm group.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE3 72-299 protein existed as one major particle group in the range of 4–10 nm, whereas apoE4 72-299 showed two major groups with a particle size of 5.1 nm (62%) and another in the range of 10.0–25.0 nm (36%).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 72–299 -> apoE4 72–299) -> (appearance of a larger apoE particle population)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 72–299; 1.0 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; dynamic light scattering at 20°C, 30–40 minutes per sample.
rows.Data location: Results, Dynamic light scattering of apoE proteins, final sentence

rows.Finding description: At 0.15 mg/ml, full-length apoE4 had a smaller large-species fraction than apoE3, 11% versus 15%, although their overall sedimentation distributions were described as very similar.
rows.Finding quote: Size distribution of apoE3 and apoE4 full-length proteins showed very similar patterns ( Fig. 4, A and B ).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (lower fraction of large apoE species at 0.15 mg/ml)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human full-length apoE3 and apoE4, expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3), with C-terminal His tags; lipid-free PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C and 40,000 rpm, continuous c(s) analysis. No cells or endo-lysosomal localization.
rows.Data location: Fig 4A–B; Table 2, full-length proteins at 0.15 mg/ml; Table 1

rows.Finding description: At 0.15 mg/ml, apoE4 72–299 had a smaller large-species fraction than apoE3 72–299, 7% versus 13%, although its overall weight-average sedimentation was higher, 6.4 versus 5.5 S.
rows.Finding quote: After calculating the integration by SEDFIT, both apoE 72-299 proteins showed four species at 0.15 mg/ml protein concentration ( Table 2 ).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 72–299 -> apoE4 72–299) -> (lower large-species fraction but higher overall sedimentation at low concentration)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 72–299, deleting N-terminal helices 1 and 2; 0.15 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C.
rows.Data location: Fig 4E–F; Table 2, 0.15 mg/ml rows; Table 1

rows.Finding description: At 1.00 mg/ml, the paper reports 10 resolved species for apoE4 72–299 versus five for apoE3 72–299, indicating greater apoE4 distribution complexity.
rows.Finding quote: However, when the protein concentration was increased to 1.00 mg/ml, 10 species were found in apoE4 72-299 protein, compared with five species of apoE3 72-299 ( Fig. 4, E and F ).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 72–299 -> apoE4 72–299) -> (more resolved sedimenting species)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 72–299; 1.00 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C; distribution regularization confidence 0.68.
rows.Data location: Fig 4E–F; Results, Size distribution of N-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins

rows.Finding description: ApoE4 1–231 had a lower fitted monomer–tetramer dissociation constant than apoE3 1–231, 16 ± 1.3 versus 29 ± 2.8 nM, consistent with stronger tetramerization; isoform-comparison significance was not reported.
rows.Finding quote: The K d of apoE3 1-191 (556 ± 233 nM) was 19 times larger than that of apoE3 1-231 (29 ± 2.8 nM) and 37 times in the case of apoE4 isoforms (592 ± 323 nM of apoE4 1-191 and 16 ± 1.3 nM of apoE4 1-231 ). Both apoE3 1-231 and apoE4 1-231 showed greater tendency toward tetramerization.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 1–231 -> apoE4 1–231) -> (lower modeled tetramer dissociation constant)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 1–231 in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C fitted with the SEDPHAT monomer–tetramer rapid self-association model.
rows.Data location: Results, Size distribution of C-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins, dissociation-constant paragraph

rows.Finding description: Raising concentration from 0.15 to 1.00 mg/ml reduced the large-species fraction of both 41–299 fragments, from 14% to 10% for apoE4 and from 10% to 9% for apoE3.
rows.Finding quote: However, both apoE 41-299 proteins showed less large species of s > 10 (decreased 1–4%). Neither apoE3 41-299 nor apoE4 41-299 therefore showed a tendency to aggregate.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 41–299 -> apoE4 41–299) -> (no greater concentration-dependent aggregation)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 41–299; 0.15 and 1.00 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C.
rows.Data location: Fig 4C–D; Table 2; Results, Size distribution of N-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins

rows.Finding description: At 0.15 mg/ml, both apoE3 1–191 and apoE4 1–191 were predominantly monomeric with some tetramer, with no significant isoform difference reported.
rows.Finding quote: Both apoE3 and E4 N-terminal domain (1–191) existed with monomers as the major component together with some tetramer.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 1–191 -> apoE4 1–191) -> (no significant change in monomer/tetramer distribution reported)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 1–191; 0.15 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity and c(s)/c(M) analysis at 20°C; estimated species masses approximately 22 and 85 kDa.
rows.Data location: Fig 5A–D, solid curves; Results, Size distribution of C-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins

rows.Finding description: Both apoE3 1–231 and apoE4 1–231 retained monomer and tetramer populations, with no significant isoform difference reported, while adding residues 192–231 increased tetramerization in both.
rows.Finding quote: The two-species distribution was still maintained in the case of the apoE3 1-231 and apoE4 1-231 ( dashed lines in Fig. 5, A and C ), whereas the s values were shifted to 2.4 and 5.5 and the ratio of the two species also changed.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 1–231 -> apoE4 1–231) -> (no significant change in monomer/tetramer distribution reported)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 1–231; 0.15 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity and c(s)/c(M) analysis at 20°C; estimated masses approximately 30–35 and 110–140 kDa.
rows.Data location: Fig 5A–D, dashed curves; Results, Size distribution of C-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins

rows.Finding description: The authors report that neither 1–271 fragment showed a significant tendency to aggregate at higher concentration. They give no statistical comparison of the two concentration responses.
rows.Finding quote: However, they did not show a significant tendency to aggregate at higher protein concentration (data not shown).
rows.Finding summary: No significant concentration-dependent aggregation was reported for either 1–271 fragment.
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 1–271; sedimentation-velocity concentration comparison in PBS, pH 7.3, at 20°C; associated experiments used 0.15 and 0.50 mg/ml.
rows.Data location: Results, Size distribution of C-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins, final sentence; data not shown

rows.Finding description: Monomer–tetramer modeling gave similar dissociation constants for apoE3 1–191 and apoE4 1–191, 556 ± 233 and 592 ± 323 nM, with no significant isoform variation reported.
rows.Finding quote: The K d of apoE3 1-191 (556 ± 233 nM) was 19 times larger than that of apoE3 1-231 (29 ± 2.8 nM) and 37 times in the case of apoE4 isoforms (592 ± 323 nM of apoE4 1-191 and 16 ± 1.3 nM of apoE4 1-231 ).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 1–191 -> apoE4 1–191) -> (no significant change in tetramerization affinity reported)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 1–191 in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C fitted with the SEDPHAT monomer–tetramer rapid self-association model.
rows.Data location: Results, Size distribution of C-terminal truncated apoE3 and apoE4 proteins, dissociation-constant paragraph

rows.Finding description: At 0.15 mg/ml, apoE4 41–299 had a larger broad large-species fraction than apoE3 41–299, 14% versus 10%, while its weight-average sedimentation was lower, 3.7 versus 4.4 S.
rows.Finding quote: After calculating the integration by SEDFIT, five species were identified for both apoE 41-299 proteins ( Table 2 ).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 41–299 -> apoE4 41–299) -> (higher large-species fraction but lower overall sedimentation)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 41–299, deleting N-terminal helix 1; 0.15 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C and 40,000 rpm.
rows.Data location: Fig 4C–D; Table 2, 0.15 mg/ml rows; Table 1

rows.Finding description: At 1.00 mg/ml, apoE4 41–299 had a large-species fraction of 10% versus 9% for apoE3, and their two major species comprised 72% versus 77%; neither fragment showed a concentration-dependent aggregation tendency.
rows.Finding quote: At an initial protein concentration of 1.00 mg/ml, the major species of apoE3 41-299 with s = 3.7 and 5.0 accounted for 77% of the total amount. In the case of apoE4 41-299 , the major species with s = 3.6 and 5.1 constituted 72% of the total protein amount.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 41–299 -> apoE4 41–299) -> (slightly higher large-species fraction at 1.00 mg/ml)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3 and apoE4 residues 41–299; 1.00 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20°C and 40,000 rpm.
rows.Data location: Fig 4C–D; Table 2, 1.00 mg/ml rows

rows.Finding description: At 0.50 mg/ml, apoE4 72–299 had a higher weight-average sedimentation coefficient than apoE3 72–299, 6.9 versus 5.7 S.
rows.Finding quote: Finally, the s w of the apoE4 72-299 protein had significantly increased (from 6.4 to 7.2) at a higher protein concentration, but apoE3 72-299 did not.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 72–299 -> apoE4 72–299) -> (higher weight-average sedimentation at 0.50 mg/ml)

rows.Finding description: Full-length apoE3 and apoE4 showed no significant difference in weight-average sedimentation: 6.6 versus 6.3 S at 0.15 mg/ml and 6.5 versus 6.5 S at 0.50 mg/ml.
rows.Finding quote: The s w values of apoE and apoE 1-271 proteins were from 6.1 to 6.6 S and did not show any significant difference.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no significant change in full-length apoE weight-average sedimentation)

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Among donors negative for both defined tau pathologies, age- and sex-adjusted analysis found no significant difference in detergent-insoluble cortical apoE between APOE4 and APOE3.
rows.Finding summary: APOE4 versus APOE3 showed no statistically significant difference in insoluble cortical apoE among donors negative for both defined tau pathologies.

rows.Finding quote: Compared to APOE3, APOE4 was associated with increased levels of insoluble apoE (FA: β = 1.24, p < 0.001) and insoluble pTau181 (FA: β = 0.72, p < 0.001), and decreased detergent-soluble tTau levels (TBSX: β = -0.18, p = 0.002).

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Fluorescent transferrin uptake imaging showed reduced internalization in human APOE4 iPSC-derived astrocytes compared with isogenic APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Using fluorescently-tagged Tf, we again observed that APOE4 astrocytes internalized less Tf than APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (reduced transferrin internalization in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human female iPSC-derived astrocytes from an APOE3 homozygous parental line and its isogenic APOE4 counterpart; early passage cells (<P8). Transferrin conjugated to AlexaFluor647 (25 μg/mL) was internalized for 5 minutes at 37°C, followed by washing, fixation and confocal microscopy. The specific Coriell parental line for this panel is not identified in the supplied text.
rows.Data location: Fig 1I

rows.Finding description: A 5-minute fluorescent-ligand uptake assay in APOE4 versus isogenic APOE3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes showed less transferrin uptake and a trend toward fewer internalized EGF puncta (n=12 samples, 30–50 cells per sample), measuring early receptor-mediated internalization without measuring recycling rate or ARF6 activity.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4 astrocytes trend towards internalizing less EGF (Figure 1G,H). Using fluorescently-tagged Tf, we again observed that APOE4 astrocytes internalized less Tf than APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less transferrin internalization and a trend toward fewer internalized EGF puncta in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived, FACS-purified astrocytes from one isogenic APOE3/APOE4 pair generated from an APOE3-homozygous parental line; study parental donors were female. Early-passage cells (<P8); fluorescent EGF (100 ng/mL) or transferrin (25 µg/mL) uptake for 5 minutes at 37°C following cooling on ice, followed by washing, fixation and confocal microscopy; EGF puncta per cell and transferrin internalization per cell quantified.
rows.Data location: Fig 1G

rows.Finding description: Representative images after a 5-minute fluorescent EGF pulse showed a trend toward reduced EGF internalization in APOE4 compared with isogenic APOE3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4 astrocytes trend towards internalizing less EGF (Figure 1G,H).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (trend toward reduced early EGF internalization in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from one isogenic APOE3/APOE4 pair with an APOE3 homozygous parental line; early-passage cells (<P8). EGF conjugated to AlexaFluor555 (100 ng/mL) was applied for 5 minutes at 37°C, followed by washing, fixation and confocal fluorescence microscopy.
